All apps and games should be accompanied by a Play Store link. No links to pirated content.

When posting an app, please share what it's about and the price. If applicable, please tell if it requires root.

Sample comment

Versa (Free - Play Store)

^Comment does not have to be exactly like that, but it should contain all of the information mentioned above.

Cheers. :D

Ascension

Play Store Link

Price: Free

Payment model: The base game is free with ads, and you can purchase additional expansions, ranging from $0.99-$4.99 each. Total cost of all expansions is $17.95(Versus $30-$40 for each of the 9 expansions in physical form, plus promo cards and small booster-pack sized expansions). Any purchase will remove ads. Expansions don't unbalance game-play, all players must own an expansion to use it in a game.

Game-play: 2-4 player deck builder. After choosing what expansions to play with, all players decks begin with the same cards. Players take turns playing their hand each turn to gain resources in order to purchase heroes, which are played from your hand, constructs, which will stick around and provide constant effects, and monsters, which are worth many points. After a certain number of points have been acquired, the game is over, and the point value of all the cards in your deck are added to the points accumulated during game-play to determine the winner. Games can be as short as 5 minutes, for 2 player games on simple expansions, or you can set the game timer to as long as 28 days. Pass-and-play multiplayer is supported, and Android users may play against iOS users(Expansion purchases are bound to Google Play or iOS App Store).

Other: The game was designed by a couple of Magic: The Gathering pro players, so balance is good and game-play is fast and fun. My name is the same in-app if you need someone to play against. There is also a physical version of the game, so if you want to play with your buddies IRL, you can. Both physical and digital copies still receive updates(Digital is one expansion behind currently).

Adding this as a reply to my other post, because Star Realms is basically Ascension in space. There are some differences, and I prefer Ascension myself, but they're both very similar and very good. The main difference is that rather than competing for resources, players directly attack each other.

Title pretty much. When submitting a link, run a query to find any other matching posts with the same URL and show all instances of that link being posted in other subverses. Add a setting to ignore any new instances of that link that come up in the future (I would have killed for this with that whole blue/gold dress mess).

This could also be useful for subverse discovery. By listing all subverses that have posts to the same link, you basically have a big web of interest (this is one of the great things about AlienTube, I can watch a Youtube video and find a bunch of subplaces I didn't know about before).

Additionally (this should be related enough), allow for URL "tagging". So if you come across an article, and know of another article or post that is very closely related, supplemental, or contradictory to the main post, you can make a connection. So say a science article is posted making damaging, false claims. The community can link to verified articles that disprove the claims so people that come across it in the future, or the next time it's posted, all of the resources are readily available.

I know it sounds a little ambitious, but I see a lot of potential for something like this. Aside from you wonderful people, there's very little reason for the everyday Joe to use Voat over reddit. These features could really consolidate a lot of content on this site and become sort of a hub for internet discovery.
Recognition of reposted content with the ability to hide it.

Such great ideas. I don't know enough about coding to know how difficult it would be to implement, but being able to see the other subverses it's posted in and/or hiding duplicate posts would be super user friendly.

I don't think implementing it is the biggest challenge. It's a pretty deep operation with a lot of searching though. So I'm willing to bet it's more taxing on the database server than anything. It would take a fair bit of money to keep up an API like that. But I work as a developer under a researcher at a university, and this sounds like something we would throw money at to get some easy network data. I don't doubt other institutions and organizations may be willing to put forth some funding as well if it took off.
